approachQuestion.prompt:
Return to the First Repeated Place

A singly linked chain starts at head. Each node has an integer value and either points to one next node or to null. Return the exact node object where following next first begins to repeat; return null if the chain ends. Values are not unique, so the answer is based on node identity, not value equality.

Constraints: 0 <= number of distinct reachable nodes <= 200,000. The structure is not modified. The supplied links remain stable during the operation.

Example 1: A(5) -> B(5) -> C(8) -> B returns node B, because B is the first node visited a second time; the equal values at A and B do not form a repeat.
Example 2: A(1) -> B(4) -> C(7) -> null returns null.
Example 3: head = null returns null. Which method returns the correct node object for every allowed chain while using the least additional storage?
constraints: The chain is deterministic: every reachable node has exactly one stable next reference, which may be null.
Node identity is available for equality checks; values may repeat arbitrarily.
Do not modify links or count the supplied nodes as additional storage.

options.text: Walk from head while storing visited node identities in a set. Before advancing, return the current node if its identity is already in the set; otherwise add it and continue. Return null if current becomes null.
options.feedback: This returns the exact first repeated node for every allowed chain and correctly distinguishes equal-valued objects. The set retains the visited identities; a two-runner method can find the same node without retaining that collection.

options.text: Advance one reference by one link and another by two links until the faster reference reaches null or both references meet. If they meet, reset one reference to head and advance both one link at a time; their next meeting is the cycle's first node.
options.feedback: The two references meet only when a cycle exists. Resetting one to the head after the first meeting makes their synchronized walk converge at the node where the repeated route begins.

options.text: Keep a set of values seen so far and return the current node when its integer value is already present.
options.feedback: Equal values on distinct nodes are not a repeated node identity. In Example 1 this returns B immediately because A and B both hold 5, even though B has not yet been revisited by following links.

options.text: Advance one reference by one link and another by two links; return null as soon as the faster reference reaches null, and otherwise return the first node where the references meet.
options.feedback: A meeting point is not generally the first node in the repeated cycle. For A -> B -> C -> D -> E -> C, the runners can first meet at D although the first repeated node is C.

feedback.reason: The answer is defined by the first repeated object along one deterministic chain. Correctness depends on node identity and, when runners meet inside a cycle, distinguishing the meeting location from the cycle's entry.
details: Move one reference one link and another two links at a time. If the faster reference reaches null, the chain ends. If the references meet, leave one at the meeting location and move the other back to head. Advance both one link at a time; their first synchronized meeting is the node where the repeated cycle begins.

After runners meet inside the cycle, resetting one to head and moving both one step aligns their distances to the entry. Compare node identities, not labels. A null fast runner proves termination rather than a cycle.

“Walk from head while storing visited node identities in a set. Before advancing, return the current node if its identity is already in the set; otherwise add it and continue. Return null if current becomes null.”: This returns the exact first repeated node for every allowed chain and correctly distinguishes equal-valued objects. The set retains the visited identities; a two-runner method can find the same node without retaining that collection.

“Advance one reference by one link and another by two links until the faster reference reaches null or both references meet. If they meet, reset one reference to head and advance both one link at a time; their next meeting is the cycle's first node.”: The two references meet only when a cycle exists. Resetting one to the head after the first meeting makes their synchronized walk converge at the node where the repeated route begins.

“Keep a set of values seen so far and return the current node when its integer value is already present.”: Equal values on distinct nodes are not a repeated node identity. In Example 1 this returns B immediately because A and B both hold 5, even though B has not yet been revisited by following links.

“Advance one reference by one link and another by two links; return null as soon as the faster reference reaches null, and otherwise return the first node where the references meet.”: A meeting point is not generally the first node in the repeated cycle. For A -> B -> C -> D -> E -> C, the runners can first meet at D although the first repeated node is C.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed floyd-meeting-then-entry method described after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Count the returned node reference as output; supplied nodes are not auxiliary storage.
constraints: Use the worst case for both acyclic and cyclic chains.
Include temporary references and call-stack storage, if any; exclude supplied nodes and the returned reference.

feedback.reason: Meeting detection and entry recovery each require only linear pointer advances.
details: In a finite chain the faster reference either reaches null or catches the slower one within a number of advances proportional to the distinct reachable nodes. After a meeting, the synchronized walk to the entry is also bounded by that node count. The method stores only a fixed number of references.

In the worst case the chain has a long non-cyclic prefix or a long acyclic path. The method must advance through a linear number of links to establish the result; each runner advances only a constant number of times per loop iteration, and the entry phase is also linear at most.
Only the slow and fast references and a fixed number of control references are retained. There is no recursion or node collection; supplied nodes and the returned reference are excluded.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is the identity-set alternative's storage, not the fixed two-runner method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Repeatedly restarting a traversal from head can be quadratic; the fixed method advances runners through links without restarting a scan for each node.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A long acyclic chain cannot be classified without following a number of links proportional to its length in the worst case.
Iterative two-runner method with a fixed number of references; no expected-time or amortized hashing assumption.
